question.question: Can an older leader complete VerifyLeader successfully after a different leader has already committed a command in a higher term, by consuming positive replication/heartbeat replies that the voters produced before that higher-term election but that are delivered only after verification admission?
question.importance: A public authority verification that succeeds after a newer leader committed before invocation can permit a caller to serve stale state. Unlike the completed eligibility question, all remote participants here are voters; the disputed relation is the freshness of a notification relative to verification admission and authority transition.
contexts: Old leader generation and a later elected generation
Per-request reply production before verification admission
event_paths: Real election and applied prefix -> hold produced old-term replies -> isolate old leader -> later real election and committed command -> old VerifyLeader admission -> deliver held replies -> observe public future and FSM state

counterevidence: Ordinary append rejects higher reply terms; heartbeat recipient rejects older request terms when handled after its transition.
Lease and negative verification notifications can demote the old leader; the schedule must preserve these workers.
Per-worker map draining prevents duplicate registration consumption but does not explicitly compare request send or reply production time against verification admission.
A new election after verification invocation is not by itself a violation of this stricter pre-invocation authority-change proposition.
unknowns: Need actual later election and committed command before the old verification invocation in one execution.
Must establish reply production before the later election, hold all other old-leader delivery paths, and observe same-future completion.
Need validate admissible timeout settings and finite delays leave lease protection active through the measured endpoint.
question.trigger_rationale: Pipeline source reading exposes no immediate unstored-entry witness; verification notifications offer a more direct authority discriminator. Accepted map b-heartbeat and b-notify-replication consume currently registered futures when delayed replies arrive, while f-verification-notification carries no send/production epoch. A response formed before a voter changes term may pass the old request/reply comparison but no longer confirm authority at invocation.

obligation.description: In an unchanged three-voter cluster, if a different leader has already been elected in a higher term and completed a committed command before an old leader VerifyLeader invocation, that old invocation must not return success solely from earlier-term positive replies produced before the new election.

scope.description: One real cluster history with later leadership and successful Apply completed before old verification invocation. Held old-term replies may be delivered after registration; other old-leader traffic is finitely delayed or disconnected. Public verification success is the primary endpoint; stale FSM contents are optional additional observations.
assumptions: Fixed voter membership; all successful reply producers are legitimate voters.
Actual bootstrap/elections/Apply generate the prefix; no direct term/role/commit mutation.
The higher-term leader Apply.Error completion must causally precede old VerifyLeader call.
Lease and negative-response workers remain running. Controlled delays and partitions are non-Byzantine and finite; any suppressed path is explicitly described.
excluded: Liveness claim from pending verification or cutoff.

pending: Construct and execute a same-history transition and correlated public completion comparison.

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader is documented to ensure the peer is still leader and may prevent returning stale FSM data. A distinct higher-term leader with a completed committed command before invocation rules out interpreting the old node as authoritative at any point after admission. Earlier replies cannot establish the promised current authority merely by being delivered to a newly registered future. This derives a necessary rejection condition, not a requirement of successful verification on the new leader or a general linearizable-read specification.
grounding.applicability: Ordinary public VerifyLeader under fixed all-voter membership and legal delay/partition faults. The check must establish actual higher-term election and successful command completion independently of old verification output.

alternatives: If lease expires or a higher-term/negative reply reaches the old node first, it may correctly fail verification; such outcomes must remain visible.
An in-flight success from before admission alone proves no violation unless later authority was independently established before invocation.

rationale: Investigate a distinct authority-context freshness proposition on the shared notification lifecycle. The completed nonvoter eligibility proposition remains closed and unchanged. A later real election and committed write would discriminate delayed valid-at-production support from current authority.

feedback.answered: Pipeline reading confirms fresh response allocation and receiver success-after-processing, plus connection release on decoding failure. Missing Error() remains an interface discrepancy, but a partially decoded positive reply does not alone establish support for an unstored entry. Preserve that lead with a precise gap: show a legal producer/error history that changes support meaning, rather than treating the absent check as consensus corruption.
remaining: Pipeline API misuse remains source-grounded but no stronger consumer consequence is established.
The new authority-freshness question needs same-execution response production, transition, committed write, verification admission and public result.
feedback.rationale: Compare remaining directions: pipeline error safety requires a producer that undermines the successful field; heartbeat contact liveness lacks a sourced deadline; delayed verification replies have a direct public authority promise and a feasible real-cluster discriminator. Existing notification, campaign and application map objects suffice for this independent question. Preserve the completed eligibility witness and investigate freshness without changing its obligation.
